title: CISAB Chess
description: My chess program in Level II BASIC, built to play in a tournament: type in the other side's move and it answers with its own.
versionOrder: Inferred development sequence, not established dates. v01 and v02 are tape1b saves 8 and 10; v03-v07 are tape13a saves 9-13; v08-v14 are tape13b saves 1-6 and 8, each in save order. Each listing is the previous one with changes, and v03 starts from v02's code (its lines 10-57 and most of the move generator are v02's). The archive labels V2-V9 were assigned by the recovery from save order; they are not in the programs. No save is dated. Tape numbers alone do not establish chronology.

versions.label: COMPUTER CHESS · Plays itself
versions.note: The earliest recovered version: moves for every piece (bishops, rooks and queens step along angles with COS and SIN), and the computer takes the most valuable piece it can. Line 80 jumps past the human move to line 81, which turns the board around, so it plays both sides.
versions.unavailableReason: Source only. On this site the Level II BASIC player runs the last recovered version; this listing and payload remain downloadable.

versions.label: COMPUTER CHESS · You or itself
versions.note: Asks SHOULD I PLAY MYSELF and DO I GO FIRST, so a person can play the computer by typing row and column numbers.
versions.unavailableReason: Source only. On this site the Level II BASIC player runs the last recovered version; this listing and payload remain downloadable.

versions.label: COMPUTER CHESS · Tournament player
versions.note: Becomes a tournament player: WHAT COLOR ARE WE, then WHAT WAS THEIR … MOVE with a random adjective. It flashes CHEAT when the start square is not theirs, asks OK? before making a move, and promotes pawns to queens.
versions.unavailableReason: Source only. On this site the Level II BASIC player runs the last recovered version; this listing and payload remain downloadable.

versions.label: COMPUTER CHESS V2 · Fixes
versions.note: Promotes pawns only on the last row, redraws the board after CHEAT, and prints OH DAMN! when they capture.
versions.unavailableReason: Source only. On this site the Level II BASIC player runs the last recovered version; this listing and payload remain downloadable.

versions.label: CISAB · Title, ADD, attacked squares
versions.note: The C I S A B title screen. ADD at OK? lets the operator put any piece on any square. Before moving it marks every square the other side attacks (lines 2000-2030) and counts them in each move's score.
